maximum_permitted_stay: Single stay up to 3 months; cumulative visitor eVisa time is limited to 3 months in any 12-month period.
entry_count: Single entry; eVisa invalid on exit.
passport_validity_rule: At least 6 months remaining at entry and enough validity to cover the entire stay.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count is published in the reviewed official FAQ.
return_ticket_rule: Onward travel itinerary is requested for stays of 48 hours or more; no separate paid-return-ticket rule is stated.
proof_of_funds_rule: No minimum funds amount is published; bank statements should not be sent unless specifically requested.
accommodation_rule: Provide information about the place of stay for visits of 48 hours or more.
travel_insurance_rule: Full medical/travel insurance must cover the stay, treatment and air evacuation to country of residence; air-evacuation cover must be at least GBP500,000; GBP1m overall cover is advised.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: Declare specified contagious diseases currently present or suffered within the 12 months before arrival; no separate vaccination certificate is listed.
transit_rule: Transit eVisa: up to 7 days per journey; double transit applies to a return within 3 months. AIG may require a multiple-entry UK visa for Bangladesh nationals; confirm before travel.
application_channel: Apply online via the AIG eVisa portal; each traveller applies separately. Pay by card or bank transfer. Cruise passengers should confirm if their operator arranges entry.
application_fee: Visitor eVisa: GBP40 standard, GBP60 fast-track; under-12 fee GBP10. Non-refundable government fee; no VAC fee.
processing_time: 90% of applications are targeted within 21 days; all within 6 weeks. Fast-track aims for 14 days; none are guaranteed.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least six months remaining at entry and sufficient validity for the stay | JPEG face photograph clearly showing the applicant's face | Full medical/travel insurance covering the stay, treatment and air evacuation to the country of residence | Evidence of medical/travel insurance policy details | Onward travel itinerary | Accommodation details | Declaration of prior criminality, excluding minor road-traffic offences | Multiple-entry UK visa valid for outward and return journeys | Signed parental consent and parent/guardian passport biographical page | Insurer confirmation that any pre-existing medical condition is covered
review_notes: Checked 2026-11-15. The AIG eVisa FAQ says all nationalities require eVisas except listed exemptions and that AIG does not issue eVisas to 13 named nationalities; Bangladesh is not on that exclusion list. Visitor eVisa allows one stay up to 3 months and cumulative 3 months in 12 months. AIG says nationals requiring a UK visa may be required to show a multi-entry UK visa valid for outward and return journeys; the UK Home Office list includes Bangladesh, so this is recorded as an AIG discretionary condition requiring confirmation for the itinerary, not as a guaranteed requirement. Standard fee GBP40, fast-track GBP60, under-12 GBP10; non-refundable. Processing estimates are not guarantees. JPEG face photo, not passport quality; no dimensions or file size published. Fingerprints and face photo may be requested as biometrics.

maximum_permitted_stay: No universal maximum published; the Island Council approves the duration; some visitors stay six months or longer.
entry_count: One approved visit; no visa entries.
passport_validity_rule: Valid passport required; no minimum remaining validity is published.
blank_passport_pages_rule: No minimum blank-page count is published; permission is recorded by a landing stamp.
return_ticket_rule: Visitors staying on Tristan must have confirmed and fully paid return passage.
proof_of_funds_rule: Visitors staying on Tristan must have sufficient funds for the entire stay.
accommodation_rule: State the accommodation sought in the advance request; bookings are arranged through the Tourism Department.
travel_insurance_rule: Adequate insurance must cover medical treatment and evacuation to Cape Town.
yellow_fever_or_health_rule: Reviewed visitor guidance requires medical insurance including evacuation; no separate vaccination certificate is stated.
transit_rule: No separate Tristan transit visa is identified; travel is by ship or yacht. Check embarkation-country transit rules separately.
application_channel: Email the Secretary to the Administrator with purpose, dates, nationality, age, preferred vessel and accommodation; obtain Island Council approval before travel.
application_fee: No visa fee. Tristan: GBP30 cruise/GBP15 yacht. Outer islands: GBP25 incl. certificate (2026); older guide GBP20.
processing_time: No published SLA; advance Island Council approval is required; shipping may require planning more than a year ahead.
required_documents: Valid ordinary passport for the duration of the visit | Advance permission request stating purpose, dates, nationality, age, preferred vessel and accommodation sought | Island Council/Administrator approval and landing stamp on arrival | Confirmed and fully paid return passage | Adequate travel/health insurance including medical evacuation to Cape Town | Sufficient funds for the entire stay | Police certificate | Cruise passenger indemnity declaration

review_notes: Checked 2026-11-15. Local government visitor guidance says no visas are required; a valid passport, advance permission to land and landing stamp are mandatory. Visitors staying on Tristan need confirmed, fully paid return passage, adequate insurance including evacuation to Cape Town and sufficient funds; accommodation and itinerary details are requested; the Island Council may request a police certificate. No universal stay limit or processing SLA is published. Main-island charges are GBP30 for cruise passengers and GBP15 for yacht passengers. The newer 2026 visitor summary lists GBP25 for Nightingale/Inaccessible including a visit certificate, while an older 2025 ship guide lists GBP20 landing-only; this optional outer-island scope/date difference is disclosed and must be confirmed before that excursion. These are landing/harbour charges, not visa fees. No separate photo specification was found in reviewed visitor/landing guidance; individual requests remain possible.
